Description: SWE-bench Verified evaluates software engineering agents on real GitHub issues by asking the model to produce a patch that makes a provided test suite pass. The “Verified” subset contains tasks that have been manually confirmed to be solvable and reliably graded, improving evaluation fidelity over the original benchmark.
Cognitive Functions:
L1: 
L2: Planning, Logical Reasoning, Working Memory, Adaptive Error Correction (minor), Attention (minor)
L3:

Description: SWE-bench Multilingual extends SWE-bench-style repository patching beyond Python to multiple programming languages, requiring models to understand language-specific tooling, idioms, and build/test workflows. It measures cross-language software maintenance ability under realistic constraints similar to professional engineering tasks.
Cognitive Functions:
L1: Language Comprehension (minor)
L2: Planning, Logical Reasoning, Working Memory
L3: Cognitive Flexibility

Description: SWE-bench Pro is a larger and more difficult software engineering benchmark designed to be more industrially relevant and more resistant to contamination than earlier SWE-bench variants. Tasks require generating correct code changes across repositories and validating them via automated test outcomes.
Cognitive Functions:
L1: 
L2: Planning, Logical Reasoning, Working Memory, Adaptive Error Correction (minor)
L3: Inhibitory Control (minor)

Description: Terminal-Bench 2.0 evaluates agentic performance in command-line environments where the model must execute sequences of shell commands, inspect files, install dependencies, and debug failures to complete real tasks. It emphasizes robust interaction with a live environment under resource constraints and noisy feedback.
Cognitive Functions:
L1: 
L2: Planning, Decision-making, Working Memory, Adaptive Error Correction
L3: Inhibitory Control (minor)

Description: BrowseComp evaluates “browse-and-reason” agents on information-seeking questions that require searching, reading, and synthesizing evidence from web-like sources rather than relying only on parametric memory. It stresses tool-augmented reasoning, source navigation, and faithful grounding in retrieved documents.
Cognitive Functions:
L1: 
L2: Planning, Attention, Working Memory, Semantic Understanding & Context Recognition, Decision-making (minor)
L3:

Description: τ2-bench (Tau2-bench) measures how well an agent can conduct multi-turn “customer support”-style interactions while using tools/APIs and adhering to domain policies (e.g., retail, airline, telecom). Success requires correctly interpreting user goals, choosing appropriate tool calls, and maintaining policy compliance across long dialogues.
Cognitive Functions:
L1: Language Comprehension, Language Production
L2: Planning, Decision-making, Working Memory (minor)
L3: Social Reasoning & Theory of Mind, Inhibitory Control

Description: OSWorld evaluates autonomous computer-using agents in realistic desktop OS environments, where the model must complete tasks by operating GUIs (opening apps, navigating menus, editing text, managing files). It probes end-to-end perception-to-action competence, including interpreting screenshots and executing multi-step UI plans.
Cognitive Functions:
L1: Visual Perception
L2: Scene Understanding & Visual Reasoning, Visual Attention & Eye Movements, Planning, Decision-making, Working Memory (minor), Sensorimotor Coordination (minor)
L3:

Description: ARC-AGI-2 is a fluid-reasoning benchmark where models infer abstract transformation rules from a few input-output grid examples and apply them to new grids. Compared with standard knowledge-heavy tests, it is intended to better isolate generalization and novel pattern induction.
Cognitive Functions:
L1: Visual Perception (minor)
L2: Logical Reasoning, Working Memory, Scene Understanding & Visual Reasoning, Attention (minor)
L3: Cognitive Flexibility

Description: Vending-Bench 2 evaluates long-horizon agent coherence in a simulated business management setting, where the agent runs a vending machine operation over many steps and must adapt to changing conditions. Performance depends on sustaining strategy, tracking finances/inventory, and making profitable decisions over time.
Cognitive Functions:
L1: 
L2: Planning, Decision-making, Working Memory, Reward Mechanisms
L3: Self-reflection (minor)

Description: MCP-Atlas measures real-world tool-use via the Model Context Protocol (MCP), requiring models to discover tools, call them with correct schemas, manage errors, and compose multi-step workflows across multiple services. It focuses on reliable orchestration and correct integration of tool outputs into final answers.
Cognitive Functions:
L1: Language Comprehension (minor)
L2: Planning, Decision-making, Working Memory
L3: Inhibitory Control (minor)

Description: FinanceAgent evaluates agent performance on tasks typical of an entry-level financial analyst, such as financial reasoning, spreadsheet-style analysis, and producing justified recommendations. It emphasizes domain grounding, multi-step quantitative reasoning, and producing professional-grade written outputs.
Cognitive Functions:
L1: Language Production (minor)
L2: Semantic Understanding & Context Recognition, Logical Reasoning, Planning (minor), Working Memory (minor)
L3:

Description: CyberGym evaluates cybersecurity agents on tasks involving identification and (in some settings) discovery of vulnerabilities in real-world open-source projects, given realistic codebases and vulnerability descriptions. It tests whether models can reason about code, reproduce exploit-relevant conditions, and propose correct fixes or findings.
Cognitive Functions:
L1: 
L2: Logical Reasoning, Planning, Attention, Working Memory (minor)
L3: Inhibitory Control (minor)

Description: SpreadsheetBench evaluates whether models can correctly manipulate and analyze complex spreadsheets, often requiring multi-step transformations, formula edits, and structured data operations. It focuses on practical “office work” competence where correctness depends on tracking cell-level dependencies and producing precise artifacts.
Cognitive Functions:
L1: 
L2: Planning, Working Memory, Logical Reasoning, Attention, Adaptive Error Correction (minor)
L3:

Description: Humanity’s Last Exam (HLE) is a frontier, multi-domain benchmark intended to probe advanced reasoning and expert knowledge, often across multimodal inputs and long-form responses. It is designed to be difficult for models that rely on shallow pattern matching, rewarding careful synthesis and verification.
Cognitive Functions:
L1: 
L2: Semantic Understanding & Context Recognition, Logical Reasoning, Working Memory, Planning (minor), Multisensory Integration (minor)
L3:

Description: AIME 2025 consists of problems from a high school invitational mathematics competition, requiring precise symbolic manipulation and multi-step derivations. Scoring rewards exact final answers and penalizes small logical or arithmetic mistakes.
Cognitive Functions:
L1: 
L2: Logical Reasoning, Working Memory, Planning (minor), Attention (minor)
L3:

Description: GPQA Diamond is a high-quality subset of GPQA composed of challenging, “Google-proof” multiple-choice questions in physics, chemistry, and biology. It emphasizes deep scientific knowledge and careful reasoning under distractors, rather than retrieval of common facts.
Cognitive Functions:
L1: 
L2: Semantic Understanding & Context Recognition, Logical Reasoning, Working Memory (minor), Attention (minor)
L3:

Description: MMMLU extends MMLU-style evaluation across many non-English languages, testing broad academic knowledge and reasoning via multiple-choice questions. It measures cross-lingual generalization and whether competence transfers beyond English prompts and subject matter phrasing.
Cognitive Functions:
L1: Language Comprehension
L2: Semantic Understanding & Context Recognition, Logical Reasoning (minor), Working Memory (minor)
L3:

Description: MMMU is a multimodal, multi-discipline benchmark where models answer questions that require interpreting images (e.g., diagrams, charts, figures) together with text across many subjects. It probes vision-language integration and higher-level visual reasoning beyond basic recognition.
Cognitive Functions:
L1: Visual Perception
L2: Multisensory Integration, Scene Understanding & Visual Reasoning, Logical Reasoning, Working Memory (minor)
L3:

Description: MMMU-Pro is a more difficult and carefully constructed successor/variant to MMMU aimed at stronger discrimination among frontier models, often using more complex reasoning and harder visual evidence. It stresses robust multimodal understanding and reduced reliance on superficial cues or dataset artifacts.
Cognitive Functions:
L1: 
L2: Multisensory Integration, Scene Understanding & Visual Reasoning, Logical Reasoning, Attention (minor), Working Memory (minor)
L3:

Description: LAB-Bench FigQA tests whether models can answer questions about complex scientific figures from biology papers, requiring accurate reading of plots, annotations, and experimental context. It targets research-relevant visual interpretation where small misreads can lead to incorrect scientific conclusions.
Cognitive Functions:
L1: Visual Perception
L2: Scene Understanding & Visual Reasoning, Semantic Understanding & Context Recognition, Logical Reasoning, Attention (minor)
L3:

Description: WebArena evaluates autonomous web agents on realistic tasks across multiple web apps (e-commerce, CMS, forums, code hosting, maps), requiring navigation, form filling, and multi-step completion. It measures end-to-end web interaction competence, including planning, state tracking, and robust UI interpretation.
Cognitive Functions:
L1: Visual Perception
L2: Planning, Decision-making, Working Memory, Visual Attention & Eye Movements
L3: Inhibitory Control (minor)

Description: MathArena Apex is a hard mathematics benchmark designed to stress multi-step problem solving and proof-like reasoning across a curated set of challenging questions. It is intended to separate models at the high end, where success depends on sustained, correct reasoning rather than short computations.
Cognitive Functions:
L1: 
L2: Logical Reasoning, Working Memory, Planning, Attention (minor)
L3:

Description: ScreenShot-Pro evaluates GUI grounding and screenshot understanding: models must answer questions or take actions based on high-resolution images of real software interfaces. It tests whether a model can correctly interpret layout, identify relevant widgets/text, and map instructions to interface elements.
Cognitive Functions:
L1: Visual Perception
L2: Scene Understanding & Visual Reasoning, Visual Attention & Eye Movements, Planning (minor), Working Memory (minor)
L3:

Description: CharXiv Reasoning evaluates whether models can reason over figures and visual content from scientific papers (CharXiv), often requiring chart/diagram interpretation and quantitative inference. It emphasizes visual-to-symbolic reasoning and faithful extraction of evidence from scientific visuals.
Cognitive Functions:
L1: Visual Perception
L2: Scene Understanding & Visual Reasoning, Logical Reasoning, Working Memory (minor), Attention (minor)
L3:

Description: OmniDocBench 1.5 evaluates document understanding and OCR-like extraction across heterogeneous document elements such as text blocks, tables, formulas, and reading order. Metrics emphasize faithful reconstruction of structured content rather than purely semantic summarization.
Cognitive Functions:
L1: Visual Perception
L2: Attention, Scene Understanding & Visual Reasoning, Semantic Understanding & Context Recognition (minor)
L3:

Description: Video-MMMU extends multimodal evaluation to video, requiring models to integrate information across frames and time to answer questions spanning many subjects. It probes temporal grounding, tracking of entities/events, and combining visual evidence with textual reasoning.
Cognitive Functions:
L1: Visual Perception
L2: Scene Understanding & Visual Reasoning, Working Memory, Multisensory Integration
L3: Cognitive Timing & Predictive Modeling (minor)

Description: LiveCodeBench Pro evaluates coding ability on competitive-programming-like and practical programming tasks with strong controls against leakage, typically scored by automated execution against hidden tests. It emphasizes writing correct, runnable code under time-like constraints with minimal trial-and-error.
Cognitive Functions:
L1: 
L2: Logical Reasoning, Planning, Working Memory, Attention (minor), Adaptive Error Correction (minor)
L3:

Description: FACTS Benchmark Suite systematically evaluates factuality and grounding behavior across multiple factuality-related tasks, aiming to measure when models make unsupported claims and how reliably they stick to evidence. It is designed to be more robust than single-dataset factuality checks by covering diverse failure modes.
Cognitive Functions:
L1: 
L2: Semantic Understanding & Context Recognition, Attention (minor), Working Memory (minor)
L3: Inhibitory Control, Self-reflection (minor)

Description: SimpleQA Verified evaluates short-form factual question answering with an emphasis on verified ground truth and careful grading to reduce ambiguity. It measures whether models can provide correct, concise answers without drifting into hallucinated details.
Cognitive Functions:
L1: Language Comprehension
L2: Semantic Understanding & Context Recognition, Attention (minor)
L3: Inhibitory Control (minor)

Description: Global PIQA evaluates practical commonsense reasoning across many languages and cultural contexts, focusing on selecting plausible actions or explanations in everyday situations. It tests whether models’ “physical and social common sense” generalizes beyond English-centric priors.
Cognitive Functions:
L1: Language Comprehension (minor)
L2: Semantic Understanding & Context Recognition, Logical Reasoning
L3: Social Reasoning & Theory of Mind (minor)

Description: MRCR v2 (multi-round coreference resolution) tests long-context retrieval by inserting multiple similar “needle” interactions into very long “haystack” conversations and asking the model to reproduce a specific referenced answer. The 8-needle variant increases distractor density, stressing robustness to interference over long spans.
Cognitive Functions:
L1: Language Comprehension
L2: Working Memory, Attention, Planning (minor)
L3: Inhibitory Control (minor)

Description: GDPval evaluates well-specified knowledge-work tasks spanning many occupations by comparing model outputs to those of human professionals under expert judging (often via win/tie rates). Tasks emphasize producing usable work products (e.g., slides, spreadsheets, plans) with correct constraints, formatting, and rationale.
Cognitive Functions:
L1: Language Production
L2: Planning, Decision-making, Semantic Understanding & Context Recognition, Working Memory (minor)
L3: Self-reflection (minor)

Description: SWE-Lancer evaluates software engineering capability on realistic, longer-horizon coding work resembling paid contracting/freelance tasks, where agents must make correct changes in repositories under practical constraints. It aims to capture end-to-end engineering effectiveness beyond narrowly scoped bug fixes.
Cognitive Functions:
L1: 
L2: Planning, Decision-making, Logical Reasoning, Working Memory, Adaptive Error Correction (minor)
L3:

Description: Graphwalks evaluates algorithmic reasoning over graphs encoded in text, such as multi-step traversals and queries that require following edges, tracking visited nodes, and applying traversal rules. It targets structured, compositional reasoning under high distractor pressure and long contexts.
Cognitive Functions:
L1: 
L2: Logical Reasoning, Working Memory, Attention, Spatial Representation & Mapping (minor), Planning (minor)
L3:

Description: Toolathon evaluates multi-tool problem solving where models must select among tools, invoke them with correct parameters, and integrate results to complete tasks end-to-end. It focuses on agent reliability under tool errors, partial results, and multi-step workflows rather than single-call tool demos.
Cognitive Functions:
L1: 
L2: Planning, Decision-making, Working Memory
L3: Inhibitory Control (minor), Self-reflection (minor)

Description: HMMT consists of high-difficulty competition math problems (e.g., from the Harvard-MIT Mathematics Tournament) that reward deep multi-step reasoning and careful case analysis. It is useful for separating strong models because many problems require sustained derivations and error-sensitive algebraic manipulation.
Cognitive Functions:
L1: 
L2: Logical Reasoning, Working Memory, Planning, Attention (minor)
L3:

Description: FrontierMath evaluates expert-level mathematics problem solving, emphasizing problems that are difficult for current models and often benefit from tool-assisted verification (e.g., computation) while still requiring conceptual reasoning. It is intended to measure progress on the frontier of mathematical reasoning rather than routine contest items.
Cognitive Functions:
L1: 
L2: Logical Reasoning, Planning, Working Memory, Attention (minor)
L3: Cognitive Flexibility (minor)
